title: customer-network-metering-and-audit-cost-model-prd-rough
body:
Purpose
This is a working PRD draft exploring a metering-first approach for customer-managed networking telemetry and audit logs. We want a concrete cost model that ties audit retention, approval gate sampling, and network telemetry exports to clear pricing + operator UX so customers can predict bill impact when they opt into different evidence/retention policies.

Context and motivation
- Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) generate two cost axes: our ingestion/processing/storage costs and the customer's egress/ingestion costs on their side.
- Customers ask: how much will enabling full audit retention + fine-grained approval gates cost? Right now we hand-wave with "depends on volume". Need productized knobs + conservative unit economics.
- This doc ties together: audit log schemas, sampling/approval gate heuristics, retention tiers, compression/compactification approaches, and a proposed metering API for billing + quotas.

Goals
1) Define retention tiers (ambient / brief / evidentiary) and per-tier expected token/event rates and unit costs.
2) Specify approval gate sampling strategies that reduce ingested volume while preserving forensic fidelity for high-risk changes.
3) Propose a metering schema and export contract for customer-managed networking events (handshake, change, operator-action, snapshot).
4) Surface UX changes: Console toggles, projected-cost preview, and per-customer quota alerts.
5) Outline experiments to measure compression, dedupe, and incremental proof bundles in real customer workloads.

Key definitions (working)
- Event: primitive record emitted by the edge adaptor or attestation agent (JSON). Typical fields: timestamp, event_type, actor, resource, delta, evidence_refs.
- Evidence bundle: compressed, optionally-signed blob (tar+lz4 + signature) that contains payloads needed to replay a change.
- Retention tiers:
  - Ambient (14 days): low-cost, coarse index. Stores event headers and small metadata only (no payloads).
  - Brief (90 days): headers + lightweight attachments (diffs, minimal traces). Good for debugging and short audits.
  - Evidentiary (365+ days): full evidence bundles retained, immutable, signed, discoverable. Intended for compliance customers.

Proposal: Metering and unit economics
- Metering primitives (per event): header_unit, payload_unit, evidence_bundle_unit.
- Header_unit = small fixed cost (e.g., 1 unit per event) — stores indexable fields (<=1KB).
- Payload_unit = variable cost proportional to compressed payload size (per-100KB).
- Evidence_bundle_unit = per-bundle (deduped) size-based cost with a higher durability premium.
- Example pricing model (internal placeholder):
  - header_unit: $0.00002 / unit
  - payload_unit: $0.001 / 100KB
  - evidence_bundle: $0.02 / 1MB-month (for long-term storage)
- Billing signals: daily aggregates per-customer + per-route (approval gate vs audit). Quota checks at header_unit level to avoid runaway ingestion.

Approval gate sampling heuristics
- Motivation: approval gates (operator-driven changes) create a lot of high-fidelity logs. We need to keep forensic usefulness while limiting cost.
- Strategy: risk-scored sampling + event-preservation for correlated sequences.
  - Low-risk changes: sample headers at 1% and keep any evidence bundle for 7 days.
  - Medium-risk: sample headers at 10%, retain payloads for 30 days.
  - High-risk (critical infra, 3rd-party-managed): 100% retention and evidentiary bundling.
- Correlation rule: if an event is sampled but is part of a linked sequence (change -> rollback -> escalation), automatically mark all linked events for full retention. This preserves investigations.
- UI implication: console exposes "sampling policy preview" showing estimated monthly units.

Data contracts and schema (simple, for discussion)
- Event header fields we index: event_id, timestamp, source_id, actor_id, action, resource_type, change_hash, risk_score, linked_event_ids.
- Payload attachments: before/after cfg, syslogs (tail up to N KB), pcap references (not stored by default, external refs allowed).
- Evidence bundle: bundle_id, created_at, compressed_size_bytes, signature, storage_path, dedupe_key.

Storage optimizations to reduce unit cost
- Deduplication: detect identical evidence bundles across customers (unlikely) and within a customer's sliding window; use dedupe_key to avoid re-storing.
- Delta-encoding: store diffs for subsequent similar events rather than full payloads. Keep base snapshot + diffs for retention tiers.
- TTL tiers + lifecycle: move evidentiary bundles to cold storage after 90 days with higher retrieval/latency cost.

APIs and webhook hooks
- Metering API (proposed): POST /v1/metering/report -> accepts daily aggregated units (header_units, payload_units, evidence_mb) OR stream per-event headers for us to meter internally.
- Retention control API: PUT /v1/customers/{id}/retention -> set ambient|brief|evidentiary by resource/route.
- Sampling policy API: GET/PUT /v1/customers/{id}/sampling-policy -> JSON policy expressing risk thresholds and rates.
- Webhook: audit-alert webhook for quota breach, anomalous ingestion, or sampled-high-risk sequence detected.

Operator and customer UX
- Console: "Retention & Cost Preview" on onboarding flow; slider for retention tier per-route with instant unit estimate (uses historical heuristics).
- Alerts: automated monthly estimate and hard quota guardrails with admin acknowledgement flow (escalatable).
- Invoice: show breakdown: header units, payload MB, evidence MB-month, archive retrieval fees.

Experiment plan (MVP)
1) Run sampling policy A/B with two pilot customers: one high-churn infra team, one security-conscious enterprise. Measure ingestion reduction and investigation fidelity.
2) Implement dedupe + delta and measure real compression across 30 days of events (target 3–5x reduction for config churn workflows).
3) Simulate cost model in staging using 6 months of synthetic events to validate per-customer monthly estimates within ±20%.

Open questions / Risks
- Legal/compliance: will customers accept deduping across tenant data? Probably not; dedupe must be per-tenant.
- Trust question: sampling could be perceived as "throwing away evidence". Mitigation: conservative defaults and clear UI disclaimers, plus canary evidentiary hooks.
- Performance: real-time quota checks may add a small latency to edge flows; propose async ingestion with header-level fast-path.
- KMS/HSM costs: signing evidence bundles has a per-operation cost. Need to include in unit economics for evidentiary tier.

Rollout timeline (rough)
- Q2 2025: implement header-only metering + console preview; pilot with 2 customers.
- Q3 2025: sampling policies + retention API; run A/B experiments and integrate dedupe.
- Q4 2025: evidentiary bundles, archive tier, and billing integration.

Next steps / TODOs
- [Priya] finalize example unit pricing with finance to replace placeholders.
- [Marcus] prototype header-only ingestion + quota guardrails (infra spike).
- [Avery] design console "Retention & Cost Preview" mocks and copy.
- Create short checklist for SOC/compliance to evaluate evidentiary signing requirements.

Notes to self
- Keep pricing conservative so customers don't get surprise bills.
- We will likely need a per-customer ingest cap with an overage flow; design early.

Appendix: sample minimal event header (for engineers)
- event_id: uuid
- ts: ISO8601
- src: edge-adaptor-1
- actor: operator:alice@example.com
- action: firewall-rule-update
- resource: vpc-12/subnet-4/rule-7
- change_hash: sha256
- risk_score: 0.72
- linked_ids: [uuid1, uuid2]

End of draft.

Feedback welcome — intended as a conversation starter rather than final PRD.
